events.title: Swiss Confederates Defeat Charles the Bold at Grandson
events.description: Forces of the Old Swiss Confederacy dealt a major defeat to Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, at the Battle of Grandson. The battle took place in the Canton of Neuchâtel during the Burgundian Wars.
events.significance: The victory showed that disciplined Swiss infantry could beat Europe's most powerful armies. It also began the decline of Burgundian power.

events.title: U.S. Congress Bans the Importation of Slaves
events.description: Congress passed an act prohibiting the importation of enslaved people into any U.S. port or place from foreign countries. The ban took effect on January 1, 1808.
events.significance: The law ended the legal international slave trade to the United States. It did not end slavery itself, and domestic slave trading continued for decades.

events.title: Texas Declares Independence from Mexico
events.description: Delegates meeting at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted a declaration of independence for the Republic of Texas during the Texas Revolution.
events.significance: The declaration created an independent republic that lasted nearly a decade before joining the United States in 1845. Texas still marks March 2 as Texas Independence Day.

events.title: Birth of Theodor Seuss Geisel, Dr. Seuss
events.description: The author and illustrator who became Dr. Seuss was born in Springfield, Massachusetts. He went on to write and draw beloved children's books including The Cat in the Hat and Green Eggs and Ham.
events.significance: His playful rhymes and inventive characters helped millions of children learn to read. His books remain among the best-selling children's titles ever.

events.title: Birth of Mikhail Gorbachev
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev was born in the village of Privolnoye in the Russian SFSR of the Soviet Union. He rose through the Communist Party to become the last leader of the Soviet Union.
events.significance: His reforms of glasnost and perestroika, and his willingness to negotiate arms reductions, helped end the Cold War. They also set in motion the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
